docs.title: Gaming Status for Home Assistant
docs.text:
This is a powerful, unified custom integration for Home Assistant that tracks and consolidates gaming presence across Steam, Xbox Live, PlayStation Network, Discord, Playnite, and the Gaming Status Agent PC app into a single, clean dashboard sensor for each person in your household / friend group. It's super useful if you want to be able to track who is online, what they're playing, and for how long.

I started developing this as a way to have persistent sensors since I was annoyed that the Xbox and Steam sensors would regularly flutter between online/offline status, making notifications and my gaming dashboard unreliable. This evolved into making master sensors instead of simply tracking each platform independently. Over time, this has grown into a much more complex integration that now tracks game time, records the last game played, provides cover art, allows for rich notifications through Discord and much, much more.

Some of the key features are listed below.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Unified Master Sensor: Combines Xbox, PlayStation, Steam, Discord, Playnite, and Gaming Status Agent into one clean "Master Status" sensor per person.
  • Online/Offline Notifications: Receive Discord, SMS, and/or Mobile notifications when users start or finish playing a game.
  • Parental Controls: Track daily playtime and receive notifications when a limit, curfew, or age-rating threshold is reached.
  • Discord Rich Presence: Track hundreds of standalone games, emulators, and Epic/EA/Ubisoft launchers automatically by hooking into Discord's Rich Presence status. Automatically ignores custom text statuses to prevent false positives.
  • Gaming Status Agent Support: Track PC games from Amazon Games, Battle.net, EA, Epic, GOG, HoYoverse, Minecraft (Java Edition), Playnite, Riot Games, Roblox, Rockstar Games, and Ubisoft (plus your own custom game rules) with the companion Gaming Status Agent Windows app, which reports the game title, launcher, and gamertag over MQTT.
  • PC Sub-Master Sensor: Automatically aggregates Gaming Status Agent, Steam, Playnite, and Discord tracking into a single, unified "PC" status. It features smart platform yielding (e.g., Discord quietly steps aside if Steam is tracking the same game) to eliminate double-counting in your playtime analytics.
  • Smart Ghosting Protection: Prevents echo sessions on a shared PC — e.g., when the Windows Xbox app incorrectly broadcasts another player's game (on Steam, PlayStation, or their own Xbox) as its own. Configured on the authoritative player (pick which other players' Xbox sensors to suppress).
  • Drop-Out Protection: Built-in grace periods prevent a gamer from appearing "Offline" if their game crashes, they switch titles, or their internet briefly blips, keeping play sessions perfectly intact and avoiding unnecessary notifications.
  • Playtime Analytics: Automatically calculates session time, daily hours, and a rolling 7-day total for easy dashboard charting.
  • Clean Dashboards: Automatically sanitizes messy game titles (e.g., changes "Minecraft Launcher" to "Minecraft") and pulls high-quality cover art from SteamGridDB.
  • Advanced Exclusion Filtering: Prevent media apps (Netflix, YouTube, Spotify) or background processes from triggering gaming statuses using a global or per-player exclusions list — the same list also keeps those titles out of the optional full game library scan below.
  • Customizable Cover Art: Automatically fetches gorgeous images from SteamGridDB and passes them to your dashboard via URL and caches them locally for fast updates.
  • "Last Seen" Memory: When gamers go offline, the sensor retains their last played game and calculates exactly how long ago they were active (e.g., Last seen 3h ago: Genshin Impact (1h 37m)).
  • Custom Avatars: Automatically pulls live gamer pictures from platform APIs, with the option to override missing or incorrect images with your own local images.
  • Native Content Ratings: Look up each game's ESRB/age rating directly from Steam, Xbox, or PlayStation — no extra API key or account, and it reuses whatever credentials your existing integrations already have.
  • Native Achievement/Trophy Tracking: Pull real achievement/trophy counts, recent unlocks, and gamerscore for whatever game is currently being played, straight from Steam, Xbox, or PlayStation.
  • Full Game Library Scan: Periodically scans a player's entire game library (not just what's currently running), tracking total achievements/trophies, completion percentage, and — for Steam — playtime per game, with a manual refresh button for instant updates.
  • Public Status Page: An optional, read-only page served by Home Assistant that anyone with the link can view without logging in, showing only the players you choose, using the same cards as your dashboards.
  • Per-Player Devices: Every player's sensors and buttons are grouped under one Home Assistant device (Settings → Devices & Services) for a clean, unified view instead of a flat list of unrelated entities.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: To configure your players, notifications, and rules, click the Configure button (gear icon) on the Gaming Status integration card. This opens the main configuration hub, which is divided into nine menus. Every menu is always listed; features that can be switched off (Notifications & Reporting, Parental Controls, and Public Page) have their own on/off toggle inside their menu.

docs.title: Achievements & Ratings
docs.text:
Native achievement/trophy/rating enrichment and full game library scanning, all in one place -- every field here is always visible together, regardless of which toggles are on, so you never have to save and reopen the menu just to find a setting.

  • Enable Native Content Ratings: See Content Ratings. Off by default. Independent from achievement tracking below — Steam ratings need no credential at all, while Xbox and PlayStation each reuse the same session achievement tracking uses (Xbox's numeric age limit is still free either way, from the same official Xbox integration sensor it always was; the credential is only needed for the ESRB/PEGI text label alongside it). This same setting is also shown on the main Parental Controls screen.
  • Enable Achievement/Trophy Tracking: Adds achievement/trophy counts and recent-unlock details to the current game's Steam/Xbox/PlayStation sensor. Off by default; the recheck interval and library scan fields below only take effect once this is on. To use a different Steam key or PSN NPSSO than the official integrations', see the credential overrides under Advanced Settings.
  • Achievement/Trophy Recheck Interval: How often to re-check for newly-earned achievements/trophies while a game keeps running. Default 900 seconds (15 min), minimum 300 (5 min).
  • Enable Full Game Library Scan: Adds a Game Library sensor (plus one per tracked platform) with your full game collection — total achievements/trophies, completion percentage, and per-game details — scanned periodically in the background. Only created for platforms you already track. Games matching Global Exclusions or that player's own Exclude Games list (see Overrides & Exclusions) are skipped entirely. Off by default.
  • Library Scan Interval: How often to rescan your full game library. Default 12 hours, range 1–24.

docs.title: Advanced Settings
docs.text:
Update your API keys and fine-tune the game-matching engine.

  • API Keys & Tokens: Update your SteamGridDB API key, or your Discord Bot Token and Server ID.
  • Steam Web API Key Override / PSN NPSSO Override: (Optional) Only needed if the Steam / PlayStation Network integration isn't installed, or you want to use a different credential than the one already configured there. Leave blank to auto-detect. These are fallbacks: while the official integration supplies its own credential, that one is used instead. A new PSN NPSSO is checked with PlayStation when you save, and the form shows an error if it's rejected. The PSN override is used by native ratings, achievement tracking and library scans.
  • Same-Game Prefix Match: Game names starting with this many matching leading words (e.g. "Call of Duty ...") are treated as the same game instead of a switch. Default: 2. Set to 0 to disable.

docs.title: Custom Artwork & Colors
docs.text:
Manually assign artwork or colors to specific games using simple Game = Value lists.

  • Custom Asset Maps (Grid, Hero, Logo, Icon): Assign artwork for custom games or unrecognized titles. Fully supports web URLs and Home Assistant /local/ paths. (Example: Marvel Rivals = /local/covers/marvel_rivals.png) A matching title uses the provided URL immediately and bypasses the SteamGridDB lookup entirely, which is useful for obscure games, custom emulators, or fan art you prefer over the official artwork. URLs must point directly to an image file (e.g., .png, .jpg). Any URL can be used, including local files, but if the file is not publicly available, it will not display in notifications. 
    Marvel Rivals = https://cdn2.steamgriddb.com/hero/a31d2779e08530d0b5fdbed368c735b4.png
Halo = /local/halo.png
  • Custom Colors: Override the automatic dominant color extractor by assigning specific hex codes to games. (Example: Cyberpunk 2077 = #fcee0a)

docs.title: Global Settings
docs.text:
These variables control how the integration handles platforms, caching, and network drops across all players.

  • Enabled Platforms: Select which gaming platforms to track (Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, Discord, Playnite, Gaming Status Agent, and Custom).
  • Enable PS3 Tracking: Adds the PS3 Media Player field (see Manage Players) to PlayStation-enabled player profiles.
  • Cache Settings: Toggle local image caching (default: on), automatic vibrant color extraction (default: on), and configure background cleanup limits (Max Files, default 200 & Max Days, default 30).
    • With caching enabled, artwork is downloaded to your Home Assistant storage, making dashboard loads instant, allowing offline artwork access, and preventing broken images during internet outages. If you use Discord notifications but do NOT have an external Home Assistant URL, image attachments will fail.
    • With caching disabled, artwork is pulled directly from SteamGridDB (raw web URLs) each time a game is loaded. If you have an external Home Assistant URL, it is recommended that you enable caching.
  • Grace Periods (Network / Away / Transition): Configure exactly how long the integration waits during network drops, idle statuses, or game switches before ending a session. Defaults: 300 / 600 / 120 seconds.
    • Offline (Network) grace period: Handles total connection loss, e.g. a PlayStation losing WiFi mid-game or the Steam API temporarily going down. The player keeps showing as "Playing" and playtime keeps counting for the grace period. If they reconnect before it ends, it's as if nothing happened; if it runs out, those seconds are retroactively subtracted from their daily total and they're marked "Offline". This also factors into how long it takes to notify you that a session has ended.
    • Away grace period: How long to wait before a Steam "Away" status becomes "Offline", preventing artificially long sessions when a game is left open but not played.
    • Game transition grace period: Handles game switching while the player stays online, e.g. closing Helldivers 2 and opening Marvel Rivals, or a crash to desktop followed by an immediate relaunch. Instead of ending the session and starting a new one seconds later, the timeline is stitched together so quick swaps or crash reboots don't fracture session history into tiny pieces.
  • Minimum Session Duration: Prevents quickly opening and closing a game (like launching a launcher) from cluttering your play history. Shorter sessions are discarded from history, don't count toward playtime totals, and won't display on the dashboard. Default: 300 seconds.
  • Master Handoff Grace Period: If a player is genuinely, continuously active on two platforms at once (e.g. playing a Steam game while also idling into a console game), whichever platform is currently shown on the Master sensor keeps that spot indefinitely as long as it stays healthy — this setting only comes into play once that platform's own connection drops into its own offline-grace or ghosted state and stays stuck there continuously; only after it's been stuck for this long does a more-recently-started game on another platform get to take over the display. Prevents notification spam from a platform's brief connectivity blips repeatedly flipping which one is shown. Default: 300 seconds (5 min). Set to 0 to restore instant hand-off.
  • Session Start Confirmation: How long a newly detected game must still be reported before a session actually starts. Useful when a sensor is unreliable and briefly reports games that were never launched — without this, a flicker lasting a second creates a real session, fires a "started playing" notification, and (because the offline grace period then holds it) can even record play time. Genuine sessions are simply delayed by this long, and their start time is backdated so no play time is lost. Does not apply to Discord, which is event-driven and has nothing to re-check. Repeated flickers can otherwise chain into a session long enough to be recorded. Leave it at 0 if your sensors are well behaved. Default: 0 (off). A good starting point if you need it is 15-30 seconds.
  • Reset History: A toggle to clear all accumulated daily/weekly/all-time playtime and session history (including the recent sessions log), for every player, upon the next Home Assistant restart. Applies once, then automatically switches itself back off. Doesn't touch achievement/trophy history — use a player's own Clear achievement/trophy history option for that. Use with caution!
  • Remove Disabled Sensors: Automatically deletes orphaned sensors from the registry if their platform is un-checked from the Enabled Platforms list.

docs.title: Manage Players
docs.text:
Add, edit, or delete the gamers in your household.

  • Platform Sensors: When adding a player, you simply select their respective integration sensors from the dropdowns. The integration will automatically filter your entities to show the correct Steam (sensor.steam_*), Xbox (sensor.*_status), PlayStation (sensor.*_now_playing), Playnite (MQTT binary_sensor.*_playnite_playing_game), and Gaming Status Agent (MQTT sensor.gsa_*) entities. The Custom platform accepts any sensor whose state is the game title (or on/off), e.g. sensor.player_one_active_pc_game (see Tracking PC Games with a Custom Sensor). You can include as few or as many platforms as a player owns. Default sensor names from the platform integrations: Steam sensor.steam_playername, Xbox sensor.playername_status, PlayStation sensor.playername_now_playing, Gaming Status Agent sensor.gsa_profilename. (Note: To remove a previously assigned sensor, simply click the 'X' to clear the entity dropdown and click Submit. The integration will save the empty state and stop tracking that platform).
  • PS3 Media Player: (Only shown when a player has a PlayStation sensor configured, and PS3 Tracking is enabled under Global Settings) The PS3 predates the modern PlayStation Network status API, so it can't be tracked the same way as PS4/PS5 — instead, select its media_player.* entity (also provided by the official PlayStation Network integration). PS3 activity feeds directly into that player's existing PlayStation sensor and history, rather than creating a separate sensor.
  • Player Details: After adding a player, you can configure:
    • Session Notifications: Select notification methods separately for when this specific player starts gaming and when they stop. Note: These must be configured under Notifications.
    • Suppress other players' Xbox sensors: Configured on the player whose own sensor(s) are accurate. Pick which other players' Xbox sensors should be suppressed whenever this player is confirmed playing on any of their own enabled platforms — including their own Xbox sensor. Fixes a shared-PC Xbox app misattributing this player's session to someone else's Xbox account. Suppressed sensors ignore that same game and show xbox_suppressed: true. Only for cross-player mixups; the same player's own overlapping sensors are already handled automatically.
    • Exclude Games: One game per line (case-insensitive) to ignore for this specific player. This applies to both current-game tracking and their full game library scan (see Overrides & Exclusions for exactly how matching works).
    • Show on public page: Include this player on the Public Page. Off by default.
    • Achievement/Trophy Tracking & Library Scan (per platform): (Only shown when the matching global toggle under Achievements & Ratings is on) Per-player Steam/Xbox/PlayStation checkboxes to turn achievement tracking and the full library scan on or off for each of this player's configured platforms individually.
    • Clear achievement/trophy history: Use with caution. The last item on the screen. Permanently deletes this player's entire recorded achievement/trophy unlock history, across every platform they're tracked on. Applies once on the next reload, then automatically switches itself back off — unlike other settings, you don't need to remember to undo it.

docs.title: Custom User Avatars
docs.text:
If you want to replace the gamer avatar with one of your own or if you want to provide an avatar for a Gaming Status Agent sensor you only need to add an image to the www/gaming_status folder. The folder will need to be added manually. For your images, use JPEG or PNG images named as platform_username_avatar.ext. So, for a user named John on Xbox, it should be 'xbox_john_avatar.png', for John's Gaming Status Agent sensor, 'gsa_john_avatar.png', and for his Custom sensor, 'custom_john_avatar.png'.

Any images added manually in this way will take priority over whatever is provided by the platform integration.

docs.title: Notifications & Reporting
docs.text:
Manage where your gaming alerts and weekly reports are sent.

The integration features a powerful, built-in notification engine. You can automatically broadcast when specific players start or finish gaming sessions directly to Discord, via SMS, or straight to your Home Assistant Companion App, without needing external tools like Node-RED or complex YAML automations.

The engine uses native Home Assistant memory to prevent duplicate alerts during rapid game-switching and gives the backend time to fetch high-resolution hero art before broadcasting.

Example Discord Notifications

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Enable Notifications & Reporting: Turns session alerts and weekly summaries on or off. Your notification methods and settings are kept while it's off. To flip it without opening another screen, leave the menu dropdown on Save and return to main menu and submit.
  • Notification Artwork: Choose which fetched artwork type (Cover, Hero, Logo, Icon, or No Artwork) attaches to your notifications. Default: Cover.
  • Add Notification: Map a friendly name (e.g., "Dad's Phone") to an existing Home Assistant notify. service. It fully supports standard mobile app notifications, Discord, and SMS.
  • Discord Notification Colors: Customize the embed colors for Discord alerts (Default, Platform Colors, Game Color, or Custom Hex). Custom Hex has a separate color per event: started playing (default #00FF00), finished playing (#FF0000), parental alerts (#0000FF), and the Rich weekly report (#F1C40F).
  • Weekly Report: Send a summary of everyone's weekly playtime to your selected notification methods on a specific day and time (off by default; default time 09:00). Toggle Enabled, pick the Day and Time, and choose the destinations.
    • Report Style: Simple (a plain, unranked line per player — the original format, unchanged) or Rich (players ranked by hours with their top game(s) for the week, a real Discord embed with artwork for Discord destinations, and a sorted plain-text version for Mobile App/SMS destinations).
    • Players to Include: (Rich style only) Leave blank to include every tracked player, or pick specific players to limit the report to just them.
    • Include players with zero hours: (Rich style only) Off by default, matching the original behavior — players with no logged hours last week are left off the report.
    • Include artwork: (Rich style only) On by default — attaches the top-ranked player's top game artwork to Discord embeds.
    • Show each player's top game(s): (Rich style only) On by default. Each player's line becomes a header (e.g. 1. Josh (45h 36m)) followed by one indented line per game, e.g.: 
      1. Josh (45h 36m)
   - Far Far West (22h 3m)
   - Genshin Impact (16h 18m)
   - ULTRAKILL (14h 24m)
    • Number of Top Games to Show: (Rich style only, shown when the option above is on) How many of each player's top games to list, 1-5 (default: 1).
    • Show rank numbers / Show total summary line: (Rich style only) Both on by default, matching the original Rich format — turn either off to trim the report down.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
This feature leverages Home Assistant's native notification engine. It does not create the connection to Discord or your SMS provider for you. Before configuring this feature, you must already have your desired notification service set up and working in Home Assistant.

  • For Discord: You must install and configure the official Discord Integration.
  • For SMS: You must install an SMS integration (such as Twilio or ClickSend).
  • For Mobile: You must have the Home Assistant Companion App installed on your iOS or Android device.

Once your service is working and you can successfully call it from the Home Assistant Developer Tools, you can plug that exact service name into the Gaming Status integration!

docs.title: How to Configure Notifications
docs.text:
With Gaming Status, you can set up global notification destinations (like a specific phone or Discord channel) and assign them to individual players.

Step 1: Create a Notification

  1. In Home Assistant, navigate to Settings > Devices & Services.
  2. Click the Configure button on the Gaming Status card.
  3. Select Notifications from the main menu and click Submit.
  4. Select ➕ Add New Notification and click Submit.
  5. Fill out the notification settings (see Destination Settings) and submit to save. You can add as many methods as you need.

Step 2: Assign to a Player

  1. From the main Gaming Status configuration menu, select Manage Players.
  2. Select the player you want to edit and proceed to their Player Details screen.
  3. Under Session Start Notifications and Session End Notifications, simply select the endpoints you created from the dropdown lists.
  4. Click Submit. (Home Assistant will automatically reload the integration in the background to apply your new routes!)

docs.title: Destination Settings
docs.text:
• Name: A friendly identifier for this notification method (e.g., "Player1's iPhone" or "Family Discord").
  • Notification Type: * Discord: Sends a rich embed message complete with the game's title, session duration, and the selected artwork.
    • Mobile App: Sends a Rich Notification directly to your iOS/Android Home Assistant app, featuring the game's art directly on your lock screen!
    • SMS: Sends a clean, text-only alert suitable for standard mobile text messages.
  • Notifier: A dynamic dropdown containing all available Home Assistant notify services (e.g., notify.mobile_app_player1s_iphone, notify.discord_bot, or notify.twilio).
  • Target ID: The routing ID for the message.
    • For Discord: Paste a Server Channel ID to post publicly to a group, or a specific User ID to send a private Direct Message.
    • For SMS: Paste the target phone number.
    • For Mobile App: Mobile notifications are routed entirely by the Notifier service name, so you can leave the Target ID box blank.

docs.title: Overrides & Exclusions
docs.text:
Manually adjust game titles, ratings, and what gets tracked.

  • Game Title Overrides: Clean up messy or lengthy names. One per line, formatted as raw name = display name. (Example: Minecraft Launcher = Minecraft) The match must be exact, and the replacement happens before any API lookups or dashboard updates, so it's also the fix when cover art lookup fails due to a name mismatch. 
    RaceTheSun = Race The Sun
Call of Duty = Call of Duty: Black Ops 7
Army of TWO: TFD = Army of Two: The 40th Day
  • Title Cleanups: A list of regex patterns (or plain text, which works the same as a literal pattern) to automatically strip from game names, one per line. (Example: Tom Clancy's on one line, Sid Meier's on the next, or a pattern like (?<=Minecraft)\*.* to strip any version suffix Minecraft appends after the word "Minecraft")* Matching is case-insensitive. It's the best way to handle dynamic "Rich Presence" statuses that console integrations append to games. Invalid regex entries are skipped (and logged as a warning) rather than breaking the whole list. 
    Tom Clancy's
Sid Meier's
Marvel's
Director's Cut
Steam Edition
: Java Edition
Open Network Test
    • Regex example: a title like Minecraft* 26.2 - Multiplayer (Realms) is reduced to just Minecraft, whatever the version number becomes later, by (?<=Minecraft)\*.*. It deletes everything from the * immediately after "Minecraft" to the end of the title, without touching unrelated titles like "Minecraft Dungeons" that don't have that *.
  • Global Exclusions: Games or apps that should be universally ignored by the tracker, for every player, one per line. (Example: YouTube on one line, Netflix on the next) An excluded app forces the sensor to report "Offline", which keeps streaming apps, music players, and dashboard menus from padding out gaming hours or sending false "Online" triggers. Overrides are applied first, then Cleanups, in that order. An Override is a whole-name swap, and any Cleanup pattern still gets a chance to run against its result afterward. Exclusions are checked against both the pre-Cleanup and the fully-cleaned name, so it doesn't matter which form your exclusion entry happens to match: excluding Minecraft catches it even if a Cleanup is what produces that name from something longer, and excluding Minecraft Launcher still works even if a separate Cleanup (e.g. one that strips Launcher generally) would otherwise erase the very word that entry is matching on. Matching ignores case and punctuation (commas, colons, dashes, trademark symbols), so Marvel Rivals™ and marvel rivals both match an exclusion entry of Marvel Rivals. 
    Xbox App
YouTube
Netflix
Hulu
Amazon Prime Video
Spotify
Microsoft Store
Store
Xbox 360 Dashboard
Setting up...
Wallpaper Engine
    • These same Global Exclusions, combined with each player's own Exclude Games list (see Manage Players), are also applied to that player's Full Game Library Scan if it's enabled — an excluded title won't show up in their Game Library sensors, and won't count toward the totals, achievement fetches, or artwork lookups either. Library scan data is cached, though, so a newly-added exclusion won't disappear until the next scheduled scan — press that player's Game Library Refresh button to apply it immediately instead of waiting.
  • Content Rating Overrides: (Only shown when Parental Controls is turned on in its menu) Manually assign a rating to games your rating provider has no data for. One per line, formatted as Game = Code, using the codes E, E10, T, M, or AO. (Example: Skull and Bones = M)

docs.title: Parental Controls
docs.text:
Set automated rules based on accumulated playtime, time of day, or game content rating.

  • Enable Parental Controls: Turns screen time limits, curfews, and rating rules on or off for every player. Each player's rules are kept while it's off.
  • Player settings: Choose Edit: to configure a player's rules, or leave it on Save and return to main menu to just save the toggles.
  • Enable Native Content Ratings: Shown on the main Parental Controls screen, below the player picker — see Content Ratings. This is what actually turns the rating pipeline on; Content Rating Limit below only appears on a player's screen once this is checked and saved, since there'd be nothing for the rule to compare against otherwise.
  • Screen Time: Set distinct weekday and weekend daily minute limits.
  • Curfew: Set distinct weekday and weekend cutoff times (e.g., 22:00).
  • Content Rating Limit: Set a maximum allowed age rating (e.g., "Ages 13+"). Ratings are looked up automatically from Steam/Xbox/PlayStation's own native rating data and cached indefinitely once found for a game. If the player's active game rating exceeds the configured age, a notification is sent the moment that game starts — switching to a different over-the-limit game always sends a fresh notification, but the same game won't spam you again while it keeps running. The notification-method picker for this rule appears alongside Enable content rating limit as soon as Enable Native Content Ratings is enabled.
  • Reminder Frequency: (Screen Time and Curfew only) Set how often to repeat the notification(s).
  • Notifications: When a limit is reached, you can automatically send a notification using any of your configured methods.

docs.title: Public Page
docs.text:
An optional page that anyone with the link can view without logging in, at /gaming_status/public on your Home Assistant address (e.g. http://<your-ha-ip>:8123/gaming_status/public). It uses the same cards as Gaming Status Cards, so it looks like your own dashboards, and refreshes about once a minute, showing when it was last updated at the bottom. Sharing the link in Discord, iMessage, Slack and similar apps shows a preview with the page title, icon, and how many players are online. Gaming Status Cards doesn't need to be installed for the built-in layout: if it isn't, the page loads the latest public release of the cards. You do need it to design a mirrored dashboard view. The settings screen shows the page's full link.

The page returns "Not found" until Enable public page is on and at least one player has Show on public page checked (Manage Players → Player Details). Only those players appear, and the page's "players online" counts include only them.

  • Enable public page: Serves the page. Your Home Assistant must be reachable from the internet for people outside your network to see it (see Sharing the page outside your network).
  • Require private link: Off by default. When on, the page's link gets a secret ?key=... added, and anyone opening the plain address gets "Not found". Share the full link shown at the top of the settings screen.
  • Regenerate private link key: Creates a new key on save. Every link shared with the old key stops working.
  • Page title: Shown as the page heading and browser tab title. Default: Gaming Status.
  • Dashboard view to mirror: Design the page on any dashboard view with the cards' own editors, and the public page shows the Gaming Status cards from that view with the same settings and grouping (sections and stacks stay together). Other card types are skipped, as are cards pinned to a player who isn't public. A dedicated dashboard hidden from the sidebar works well. Leave it on Built-in default layout to have the page laid out automatically instead.
  • Default layout: general cards / cards for each player: (Built-in default layout only) Which cards to show once for everyone (e.g. player list, slideshow, leaderboard, weekly stats) and which to show grouped under each public player (e.g. Gamercard, game library, 100% completed games, near completion). Cards appear in the order listed; to reorder, remove a card and add it back to move it to the end. A per-player card is skipped for a player who doesn't have the data it needs, and the Gamercard is shown once per platform the player has a library on.
  • Exclude libraries with zero tracked achievements: (Built-in default layout only) On by default. Game library cards leave out games with no achievements earned, and are skipped (or hide a platform's tab) when a player has none at all.
  • Light or dark mode: Auto follows each visitor's device; Light or Dark forces it for everyone.
  • Theme: An installed Home Assistant theme for the page. The default uses the mirrored view's own theme if it sets one, otherwise Home Assistant's default colors.
  • Show gamertags: Off by default. When off, gamertags are removed before any data leaves Home Assistant. When on, the built-in layout shows them in the player list and Gamercards; on a mirrored view, also turn on Show gamertags in each card's editor.
  • Cards script URL: (Optional) Leave blank to use the Gaming Status Cards resource already installed in your dashboards; falls back to the latest public release if none is found.

What's never shared: Credentials, account IDs, parental control data, and (unless enabled) gamertags are stripped from the page's data. The Game Management card is never shown, and the page can't call any services or change anything. Each visitor's address is limited to 120 requests a minute, which is well above what an open page uses.

docs.title: Sharing the page outside your network
docs.text:
If you put the page behind a reverse proxy or tunnel (e.g. Cloudflare Tunnel) and only want to expose the page rather than all of Home Assistant, allow these paths:

Path Why /gaming_status/public The page itself /api/gaming_status/public.json The data the page loads Your Gaming Status Cards resource, e.g. /hacsfiles/Gaming-Status-Cards/ The cards script (match the path and capitalization under Settings → Dashboards → Resources), unless you set Cards script URL to a public copy /local/gaming_status_cache/ Cached game artwork /api/image_proxy/ Xbox and PlayStation gamerpics

Add any other /local/ folders that hold images (such as /local/gaming_status/) you've set as overrides. Home Assistant also needs use_x_forwarded_for and trusted_proxies set under http: in configuration.yaml for proxied requests to be accepted.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Go to Settings / Devices & Services and press the Add Integration button, or click the shortcut button below (requires My Homeassistant configured):

Gaming Status is configured entirely through the Home Assistant UI. There is no YAML or JSON configuration required. (Note: If you are upgrading from an older version, your gaming_profiles.json file will be automatically migrated to the new database and can be safely deleted).

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
1. In Home Assistant, navigate to Settings > Devices & Services.
  2. Click + Add Integration and search for Gaming Status.
  3. On the first screen, choose which Platforms to Track, whether to turn on Notifications and Parental Controls (both can be switched on or off later from their own menus), enter an optional SteamGridDB API Key (highly recommended for artwork; get a free key here or add it later under Advanced), and toggle Local Image Caching (pre-checked only when Home Assistant has an external HTTPS URL).
  4. If Discord was selected, a dedicated step asks for your Discord Bot Token and Server ID (see Setting up Discord Tracking).
  5. Finally, name your first player and map their platform sensors. Click Submit.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Method 1: HACS (Recommended) Installation is easiest via the Home Assistant Community Store (HACS). Gaming Status is a default repository in HACS, so you do not need to add any custom links!

Simply click the button below (requires My Home Assistant configured) to open the download page directly, or search for "Gaming Status" in HACS.

Method 2: Manual Copy the gaming_status folder into your custom_components folder and restart Home Assistant.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
This integration acts as a "wrapper" that intelligently processes data from your existing integrations. Before installing, ensure you have any necessary base integrations installed and working in Home Assistant. Not all are required, but it is recommended that you have at least ONE official integration installed. Discord and Playnite can also be used for game tracking with or without the other integrations, but they are more complicated to set up:

  • Official PlayStation Network Integration
  • Official Steam Integration
  • Official Xbox Integration

docs.title: Recommended
docs.text:
While not required for functionality, I recommend installing the following for the most robust dashboard cards and tracking:

  • SteamGridDB API Key - Provides artwork for games. This is not REQUIRED, but it is HIGHLY recommended!
  • Gaming Status Cards - Easy to use companion dashboard cards, so you don't have to make your own.
  • Official Discord Integration - Requires setting up a Discord Bot. REQUIRED if you want to use Discord for notifications but NOT required for Discord game tracking.
  • Mosquitto Broker - REQUIRED if you plan to use Playnite or Gaming Status Agent for tracking games. You will also need an MQTT add-on installed in Playnite (such as Playnite MQTT Client) to broadcast your status to Home Assistant.
  • Gaming Status Agent - A Windows tray app that detects games from numerous launchers and publishes them to Home Assistant over MQTT. REQUIRES an MQTT broker (see Mosquitto above). See Setting up Gaming Status Agent Tracking.

docs.title: Obtaining a SteamGridDB API Key
docs.text:
To display beautiful, high-resolution game covers on your dashboard, this integration requires a free API key from SteamGridDB.

  1. Go to SteamGridDB.com.
  2. Click Login in the top right corner and authenticate using your Steam account.
  3. Click your profile picture in the top right and select Preferences.
  4. Navigate to the API tab on the left menu.
  5. Click Generate API Key.
  6. Copy the generated key and paste it into the SteamGridDB API Key field during Initial Setup or under the Advanced menu.

docs.title: Content Ratings
docs.text:
If you plan to use the Content Rating Limit parental control, enable Enable Native Content Ratings (either under the Achievements & Ratings menu or on the main Parental Controls screen). It's the same setting, shown in both places for convenience. This looks up each game's ESRB rating directly from Steam, Xbox, or PlayStation, reusing whatever credentials you already have configured on the official integrations. No separate API key or account needed. This is independent from achievement/trophy tracking, so you don't need to enable that (or its heavier credential/polling requirements) just to get ratings working. Content Rating Limit's own fields only appear on a player's screen once this is on, since there's nothing for the rule to check against otherwise.

Note: native rating coverage isn't complete for every title. If a game comes back unrated, you can manually assign it a rating using the Content Rating Overrides field under Overrides & Exclusions.

docs.title: What Next?
docs.text:
Once everything is up and running (with sensors showing up from the integration), try playing a game for at least 5 minutes to make sure the online status is reflected in the _master sensors. Note that, by default, sessions shorter than 300 seconds (5 minutes) are discarded and do not count toward the total playtime hours. If the sensors are working correctly, try some of the following! If not, see the troubleshooting documentation.

  • Add some sweet displays to your dashboard, showing who's online and what they're playing
  • Set up Discord, SMS, and/or Mobile notifications for when users start, stop, and switch games
  • Add a slideshow to your dashboard or wallpanel display to see what's being played
  • Add a weekly hours chart or a per-game breakdown chart to visualize playtime trends across your household
  • Install Gaming Status Agent to track PC games from Epic, GOG, Battle.net, Ubisoft, EA, and more
  • Use a sensor to track whether or not anyone is gaming (useful for automations or contextual card display)
  • Check out other player options for features like preventing tracking of games by the wrong players and per-user game exclusions

docs.title: Attributes for Master Sensors
docs.text:
Each sensor has a set of attributes that can be utilized in dashboards charts, etc. The *_master sensors provide the following attributes:

Aggregate Analytics

Used by the Gaming Status Cards for chart rendering raw_calendar_breakdown_last_week Same as raw_calendar_breakdown, for the previous calendar week all_time_total_hours / all_time_session_count / all_time_top_games Lifetime hours, session count, and top 10 games across all platforms recent_achievements Achievement/trophy unlocks merged from every platform (newest first, capped at 30, with up to 5 reserved per platform so one platform's burst can't crowd out another) achievement_tracking_enabled / color_extraction_enabled Whether achievement tracking is enabled for any of this player's platforms / whether vibrant color extraction is on recent_sessions List of the most recently completed play sessions across all of this player's platforms (newest first, capped at 20): {game, platform, platform_key, duration_seconds, date, start_time, end_time, hero_art_url, game_dominant_color}. platform is a display label (a Gaming Status Agent session shows its launcher); platform_key is the internal platform key

Active Status

Attribute Description secondary Current state or the time elapsed and session duration of the last played game active_platform The name of the platform currently driving the status (e.g., "Steam"). For Gaming Status Agent this is the reported launcher (e.g., "Epic") active_platform_key The internal key of the platform driving the status (steam, xbox, playstation, playnite, gsa, discord), for dashboards that need to identify the platform regardless of the launcher label. The ..._pc sub-master sensor exposes this same attribute, scoped to just its own PC platforms (Playnite, Gaming Status Agent, Custom, Steam, Discord)
