docs.title: Attributes for Library Sensors
docs.text:
(Requires Full Game Library Scan to be enabled)

The sensor's state on both the summary and per-platform Library sensors is a raw count of achievements/trophies earned — not a percentage and not a game count. On the summary sensor that's the total earned across every tracked platform combined; on a platform sensor (e.g. ..._library_steam) it's earned on that platform only. The rest of the picture — totals, percentages, game counts — lives in the attributes below.

Summary Sensor (..._library_summary)

Attribute Description total_achievements_possible Sum of every achievement/trophy that exists across all tracked games, on all platforms total_gamerscore Total Xbox gamerscore earned, summed across all Xbox games total_platinum_trophies Total PlayStation platinum trophies earned, summed across all PlayStation games average_completion_percent Average per-game completion percentage across every tracked game on every platform game_count Total number of games tracked across all platforms tracked_platforms List of platforms included in this scan (e.g. ["steam", "xbox"]) last_sync_success true if the most recent scan completed with no errors on any platform platform_errors "None" if the last scan was clean, otherwise a dict of {platform: error message} for any platform whose scan failed (e.g. rate-limited, network error, credentials not configured) last_synced Timestamp of the most recent completed scan games Full list of every tracked game across all platforms — see below for each entry's shape achievement_backfill_pending / achievement_backfill_total / achievement_backfill_complete Progress of the Xbox/PlayStation achievement backfill (titles still pending, titles total, and whether it's done) achievement_backfill_by_platform The same progress broken out per platform: {xbox: {pending, total}, playstation: {pending, total}}

Paced backfill: Per-game achievement details on Xbox and PlayStation are fetched gradually in the background, every 15 minutes. A small batch per player (8 Xbox / 5 PlayStation titles), staggered between players, is used to stay within platform rate limits; a title that fails 5 times is skipped. Steam refreshes a rotating slice of the library each scan instead. A large library can therefore take a while to fully populate.

Steam account check: Each Steam library remembers which Steam account it was scanned from. If that changes (or on the first scan after updating from a version that didn't record it), games that aren't in the current account's library are dropped instead of kept. This cleans up libraries where an older version mixed in games from the Steam API key owner's account.

Platform Sensors (..._library_steam, ..._library_xbox, ..._library_playstation)

Attribute Description achievements_total Sum of every achievement/trophy that exists across this platform's tracked games game_count Number of games tracked on this platform games List of games on this platform — see below for each entry's shape playtime_hours (Steam only) Total hours played across every owned Steam game, summed from Steam's own playtime data gamerscore_earned / gamerscore_total (Xbox only) Total gamerscore earned / possible, summed across all Xbox games trophies_bronze / trophies_silver / trophies_gold / trophies_platinum (+ _total variants) (PlayStation only) Trophy counts earned / possible, per tier, summed across all PlayStation games

Each entry in a games list

Field Description title Game name platform steam, xbox, or playstation id Platform-specific game identifier (Steam appid, Xbox title_id, or PSN npCommunicationId) achievements_earned / achievements_total Earned / possible achievements or trophies for this game percent Completion percentage for this game, 0.0 if the game has no achievements/trophies at all playtime_hours (Steam only) Hours played, from Steam's own playtime data gamerscore_earned / gamerscore_total (Xbox only) Gamerscore earned / possible for this game trophies_earned / trophies_total (PlayStation only) Dicts of {bronze, silver, gold, platinum} counts earned / possible game_cover_art / game_hero_art / game_logo_art / game_icon_art Artwork URLs from SteamGridDB, if configured

docs.title: Attributes for Players Online Sensor
docs.text: Attribute Description active_games A comma-separated string of the games currently being played by online players

docs.title: Note
docs.text: Several of these attributes (e.g., artwork URLs, breakdown dictionaries, session detail dicts, play_history, and recent_sessions) are explicitly added to _unrecorded_attributes in the sensor classes. This is a deliberate performance optimization to prevent Home Assistant from saving these frequently-changing or large values into the long-term database (recorder), which keeps your database file from growing excessively large.

docs.title: Device Page Settings
docs.text:
Common settings can also be changed from each player's device page (Configuration section), from a dashboard, or in automations, without opening Configure. These controls read and write the same settings as Configure, so a change in either place shows up in the other.

Per player

Setting Control Applies Screen time limit On/off Immediately Weekday screen time, Weekend screen time Minutes Immediately Screen time warning Slider, minutes before the limit (0 = off). Fires the Screen time warning event Immediately Screen time reminder interval Once per day, or every 15, 30 or 60 minutes Immediately Curfew On/off Immediately Weekday curfew, Weekend curfew Time Immediately Curfew reminder interval Once per day, or every 15, 30 or 60 minutes Immediately Rating limit, Maximum age rating On/off, and Everyone through Adults Only. Only while Native Content Ratings is on Immediately Steam / Xbox achievement tracking, PlayStation trophy tracking On/off, one per platform the player has. Only while Achievement/Trophy Tracking is on Reloads Gaming Status Steam / Xbox / PlayStation library scan On/off, one per platform. Only while Full Game Library Scan is on Reloads Gaming Status Show on public page On/off Immediately

On the Gaming Status hub device: Public page, Notifications, Parental controls and Weekly report on/off, all applied immediately.

Parental controls follow their rules. A player's parental controls only appear while they'd do something:

  • Screen time limit, Curfew and Rating limit are available while Parental controls is on.
  • Each rule's other controls (its times, minutes, warning and reminder interval) are available only while that rule is on.

Turning a rule on or off in Configure shows or hides its controls straight away. Turning it on or off from its own switch takes about 30 seconds, because Home Assistant briefly reloads Gaming Status to add or remove them. If you disable one of these controls yourself (for example, to keep it out of reach of other people in your home), Gaming Status leaves it disabled.

Who can change these: anyone who can use your Home Assistant dashboards can change an enabled control, while Configure is limited to administrators. If players have their own Home Assistant accounts, disable any parental control you don't want them to change, or keep it off your dashboards.

Notification destinations, and the action each parental rule takes, are only set in Configure.

docs.title: Devices
docs.text:
Every player gets their own Home Assistant Device (Settings → Devices & Services → Gaming Status → Devices), named after the player and grouping all of their entities together — platform sensors, the Master and PC sub-master sensors, Game Library sensors, and their Game Library Refresh button all live under one device page, instead of a flat list of unrelated entities. The device's "model" field lists whichever platforms that player has configured (e.g. "Steam + Xbox").

The two entities that aren't tied to any single player — Players Online and Anyone Gaming — are grouped under a separate, shared Gaming Status hub device instead.

Deleting a player from Manage Players removes their entire device (and everything on it) in one go.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
Upon restart, the integration will instantly read your settings and generate the master tracking sensors for your dashboard. All entities generated by the integration are strictly standardized under the gaming_status_ namespace.

Entity Type Description sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_steam Sensor Steam sensor for each added profile sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_xbox Sensor Xbox sensor for each added profile sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_playstation Sensor PlayStation sensor for each added profile sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_discord Sensor Discord sensor for each added profile sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_playnite Sensor Playnite sensor for each added profile sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_gsa Sensor Gaming Status Agent sensor for each added profile sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_custom Sensor Custom sensor for each added profile sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_pc Sensor Sub-master sensor that automatically aggregates Steam, Discord, Playnite, Gaming Status Agent, and Custom into a single unified PC state sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_master Sensor Master sensor for each added profile that combines all added platforms into one "Online/Offline" status sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_library_summary Sensor (Requires Full Game Library Scan) Game Library summary sensor per profile, combining every tracked platform sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_library_steam Sensor (Requires Full Game Library Scan) Steam-specific Game Library sensor sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_library_xbox Sensor (Requires Full Game Library Scan) Xbox-specific Game Library sensor sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_library_playstation Sensor (Requires Full Game Library Scan) PlayStation-specific Game Library sensor event.gaming_status_XXXXX_session Event Gaming Activity: the player's latest event. Its event_type attribute is started, switched, stopped, screen_time_warning, screen_time_exceeded, curfew_exceeded, rating_exceeded or achievement_unlocked, and its other attributes are that event's data. See Events image.gaming_status_XXXXX_game_art Image Cover art of the game the player is playing, or last played. Works in picture cards and notifications button.gaming_status_XXXXX_library_refresh Button (Requires Full Game Library Scan) Manually triggers an immediate full library rescan for this player, bypassing the normal scan interval sensor.gaming_status_players_online Sensor Global sensor that tracks the total number of players currently online binary_sensor.gaming_status_anyone_gaming Binary Sensor Useful for showing or hiding cards and for automations. See below button.gaming_status_send_weekly_report_now Button (Requires Weekly Report to be enabled) Manually sends the weekly report immediately, using its current settings and destinations -- handy for previewing the exact formatting without waiting for its scheduled day/time

docs.title: The "Is Anyone Gaming?" Binary Sensor (For Automations)
docs.text:
The Problem: You want to trigger a Home Assistant automation (like changing the living room lights to a specific color, or silencing TTS announcements) whenever anyone in the house starts gaming, but you don't want to write a messy automation trigger that manually lists every single person's Xbox, Steam, PlayStation, Discord, Playnite, and Gaming Status Agent sensors.

The Solution: binary_sensor.gaming_status_anyone_gaming automatically searches your entire Home Assistant system for any Master Gaming Sensors (_master) created by this integration. If any of them are currently playing a game, it turns on. When the last person stops playing, it turns off.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Gaming Status fires these events on the Home Assistant event bus, for use as automation triggers. They use the same filtering as notifications, so a launcher handing off to the real game, or a game moving from one platform to another, doesn't fire extra events. They fire whether or not notifications are turned on.

Event When Data gaming_status_session_started A player starts a new gaming session player, game, platform, entity_id (the master sensor), device_id, game_cover_art, game_color gaming_status_session_switched A player switches from one game to another The same fields for the new game, plus previous_game and duration_minutes (how long the previous game was played) gaming_status_session_ended A player stops playing The same fields for the game that ended, plus duration_minutes gaming_status_screen_time_warning A player has played to within their Screen time warning minutes of the limit (once per day; set the minutes in Parental Controls or with the player's Screen time warning entity) player, entity_id, device_id, game, limit_minutes, minutes_played, minutes_left gaming_status_screen_time_exceeded A player reaches their daily screen time limit while playing. Repeats on the rule's Repeat interval while they keep playing player, entity_id, device_id, game, limit_minutes, minutes_played, minutes_over gaming_status_curfew_exceeded A player is still playing at curfew. Repeats on the rule's Repeat interval while they keep playing player, entity_id, device_id, game, curfew (e.g. 22:00), minutes_over gaming_status_rating_exceeded A player starts a game rated above their limit (once per game) player, entity_id, device_id, game, age_floor, esrb, pegi, max_age_floor (the player's limit), game_cover_art gaming_status_achievement_unlocked A player earns an achievement or trophy player, entity_id, device_id, game, platform, console, achievement, description, tier (PlayStation trophy tier), icon_url, unlocked_at, game_color
  • message: Every event also includes a ready-made sentence starting with the player's name, such as "Bob stopped playing Borderlands 4 (3h 4m)", "Susan has 15 minutes of screen time left" or "Steve unlocked platinum trophy "Platinum" in Astro Bot". Use it as-is in a notification: {{ trigger.message }} with a Gaming Status trigger, or {{ trigger.event.data.message }} with an event trigger.
  • game_color: The game's dominant color as a hex code (e.g. #3c3c5a), handy for setting light colors. Only filled in when Enable Game Color Extraction is turned on in Global Settings; otherwise it's empty. Gaming Status waits up to about 15 seconds after a game starts for its artwork and color, so they're almost always included.
  • Parental events only fire for rules that are turned on under Parental Controls, but they fire whether or not the rule has an action or notification destination set, so you can build your own response in an automation.
  • Achievement events arrive when Gaming Status next checks for unlocks (every 15 minutes by default, set by Achievement/Trophy Recheck Interval), since Steam, Xbox and PlayStation don't announce unlocks as they happen. Only unlocks from the last hour fire an event, so turning on achievement tracking or a library scan filling in older history doesn't set off a flood of events. Requires Enable Achievement/Trophy Tracking.
  • A switch within 90 seconds of starting a game (e.g. a launcher opening the real game) fires nothing; the earlier Started playing stands.

Each event is also written to Home Assistant's Logbook in plain language, for example "Charlie started playing ELDEN RING on Steam", "Jill switched from Halo (1h 35m) to DOOM Eternal on Xbox", "Tommy is still playing Roblox after the 22:00 curfew (10 minutes past)" or "Greg unlocked "Arena Grande" in Borderlands 4". These entries appear in the Logbook and on each player's device and master sensor pages.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
In the automation editor's Add trigger dialog, the events are available as Started playing, Switched games, Stopped playing, Screen time warning, Screen time exceeded, Curfew exceeded, Rating exceeded and Achievement unlocked. Find them under By type → Gaming Status, or under By target by picking a player (their device is under Unassigned → Devices unless you've given it an area). Each player's device also has matching classic device triggers.

The target picks which player(s) the trigger watches, not which sensor. Any of a player's Gaming Status sensors works: picking their Library or Steam sensor triggers exactly the same as picking their master sensor, because the trigger looks up the player that sensor belongs to. The master sensor (Name Gaming Status) is the clearest choice. You can also target a player's device (device_id:), or an area or label (area_id: / label_id:) to cover several players at once.

Home Assistant version: These triggers need Home Assistant 2025.12 or newer, and they appear in the Add trigger dialog from 2026.2. On older versions they aren't available, but the events above and the classic device triggers still work, so use an event trigger (see the second example below) instead.

With these triggers, the event data is directly under trigger. (e.g. trigger.game_color). With a raw event trigger, it's under trigger.event.data..

docs.title: Example: light matches the game's color
docs.text:
Sets a light to the game's color whenever Adam starts playing or switches games:

alias: Game color lighting
triggers:
  - trigger: gaming_status.session_started
    target:
      entity_id: sensor.gaming_status_adam_master
    options: {}
  - trigger: gaming_status.session_switched
    target:
      entity_id: sensor.gaming_status_adam_master
    options: {}
conditions:
  # Skip games with no extracted color (or Enable Game Color Extraction off).
  - condition: template
    value_template: "{{ trigger.game_color is string }}"
actions:
  - action: light.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: light.game_room
    data:
      brightness_pct: 80
      rgb_color: >
        {% set c = trigger.game_color.lstrip('#') %}
        {{ [c[0:2] | int(base=16), c[2:4] | int(base=16), c[4:6] | int(base=16)] }}
mode: restart

docs.title: Example: the same thing with an event trigger
docs.text:
Useful in YAML packages or when you'd rather match on event data, such as a specific player or game:

alias: Game color lighting (event)
triggers:
  - trigger: event
    event_type: gaming_status_session_started
    event_data:
      player: Adam
  - trigger: event
    event_type: gaming_status_session_switched
    event_data:
      player: Adam
conditions:
  - condition: template
    value_template: "{{ trigger.event.data.game_color is string }}"
actions:
  - action: light.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: light.game_room
    data:
      brightness_pct: 80
      rgb_color: >
        {% set c = trigger.event.data.game_color.lstrip('#') %}
        {{ [c[0:2] | int(base=16), c[2:4] | int(base=16), c[4:6] | int(base=16)] }}
mode: restart

Remove the event_data lines to react to every player.

docs.title: Example: a whole gaming setup
docs.text:
Turns a gaming setup on when Adam starts playing, keeps the light matched to whatever game he's playing, and turns everything off when he stops:

alias: Gaming setup
triggers:
  - trigger: gaming_status.session_started
    target:
      entity_id: sensor.gaming_status_adam_master
    options: {}
    id: started
  - trigger: gaming_status.session_switched
    target:
      entity_id: sensor.gaming_status_adam_master
    options: {}
    id: switched
  - trigger: gaming_status.session_ended
    target:
      entity_id: sensor.gaming_status_adam_master
    options: {}
    id: ended
variables:
  # The game's color as [r, g, b], or white if it has none.
  rgb: >
    {% set c = (trigger.game_color or '') | replace('#', '') %}
    {% if c | length == 6 %}
      {{ [c[0:2] | int(base=16), c[2:4] | int(base=16), c[4:6] | int(base=16)] }}
    {% else %}
      {{ [255, 255, 255] }}
    {% endif %}
actions:
  - choose:
      - conditions:
          - condition: trigger
            id: started
        sequence:
          - action: switch.turn_on
            target:
              entity_id: switch.gaming_pc_power
          - action: light.turn_on
            target:
              entity_id: light.game_room
            data:
              brightness_pct: 80
              rgb_color: "{{ rgb }}"
      - conditions:
          - condition: trigger
            id: switched
        sequence:
          - action: light.turn_on
            target:
              entity_id: light.game_room
            data:
              rgb_color: "{{ rgb }}"
      - conditions:
          - condition: trigger
            id: ended
        sequence:
          - action: switch.turn_off
            target:
              entity_id: switch.gaming_pc_power
          - action: light.turn_off
            target:
              entity_id: light.game_room
mode: single

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Beyond the dashboard, Gaming Status exposes five Home Assistant services (Developer Tools → Actions, or callable from automations/scripts) for cleaning up a player's stored game history after the fact — useful when a data source ever misreports a game's name (e.g. DOOM Eternal In the menu instead of DOOM Eternal) or when you simply want to remove a game's history entirely, or to fix individual sessions.

gaming_status.rename_game Renames a game across a player's stored history (recent sessions, daily/weekly breakdowns, and archived per-day totals), merging its playtime into an existing name if one already matches. Does not rename a currently in-progress session — the fix applies once that session ends naturally.

Field Required Description player Yes The player's configured name, e.g. Player1 platform No Limit the rename to one platform (steam, xbox, playstation, playnite, gsa, discord). Omit to apply across all of the player's platforms old_name Yes The exact game name currently stored, e.g. DOOM Eternal In the menu new_name Yes The name to rename it to, e.g. DOOM Eternal

gaming_status.delete_game Permanently purges every trace of a named game from a player's stored history — every recorded session, today's live totals, every archived day's contribution to daily/weekly breakdowns, and any recorded achievement/trophy unlocks for that game. This cannot be undone.

Field Required Description player Yes The player's configured name, e.g. Player1 platform No Limit the deletion to one platform. Omit to purge across all of the player's platforms game Yes The exact game name to delete

gaming_status.delete_session Permanently removes one specific recorded session, correcting only that session's contribution to daily/weekly/lifetime totals. Only works for sessions still in that sensor's recent_sessions list.

Field Required Description player Yes The player's configured name platform No Limit the search to one platform. Omit to search all of the player's platforms game Yes The session's game name start_time Yes The session's exact start_time (ISO timestamp), as shown in recent_sessions

gaming_status.add_session Manually inserts a completed session (e.g. to backfill play that was never tracked), updating totals the same way a tracked session would.

Field Required Description player Yes The player's configured name platform Yes Exactly one platform to add the session to, e.g. steam game Yes The game name start_time Yes ISO timestamp the session started end_time Yes ISO timestamp the session ended (must be after start_time)

gaming_status.reassign_session Moves one recorded session to another player (and/or platform), correcting totals on both ends — useful when the wrong account was signed in on a shared console or app.

Field Required Description from_player Yes The player the session is currently attributed to from_platform No Limit the search to one of from_player's platforms game Yes The session's game name start_time Yes The session's exact start_time, as shown in the source sensor's recent_sessions to_player Yes The player to move the session to to_platform Yes Exactly one platform on to_player to move it onto

The rename and delete services can also be triggered from a dashboard using the Game Management card, which provides player/platform/game dropdowns populated from real data instead of requiring you to type exact names.

docs.title: Voice Assistants (Assist)
docs.text:
Gaming Status adds three questions you can ask Home Assistant's Assist:

Question Example answer Who's playing games? "Adam is playing ELDEN RING on Steam, and Josh is playing Halo on Xbox." What is player playing? "Adam is playing ELDEN RING on Steam." or "Adam isn't playing anything right now. The last game was Halo." How long has player played? "Adam has played 2 hours and 15 minutes today and 9 hours this week."

AI-powered assistants (OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Ollama and others set to control Home Assistant): these work automatically, once at least one player's master sensor is exposed to the assistant (Settings → Voice assistants → Expose). Ask in your own words.

Home Assistant's built-in assistant only understands sentences it has been taught. Create custom_sentences/en/gaming_status.yaml in your Home Assistant config folder with the following, then restart:

language: "en"
intents:
  GamingStatusWhoIsPlaying:
    data:
      - sentences:
          - "who is (playing [video] games|gaming)"
          - "who's (playing [video] games|gaming)"
          - "is anyone (playing [video] games|gaming)"
  GamingStatusWhatIsPlaying:
    data:
      - sentences:
          - "what is {player} playing"
          - "what's {player} playing"
          - "what game is {player} playing"
  GamingStatusPlayTime:
    data:
      - sentences:
          - "how long has {player} (played|been playing|been gaming) [today|this week]"
          - "how much has {player} played [today|this week]"
lists:
  player:
    wildcard: true

Player names are matched without regard to capitalization, so "what is adam playing" works for a player named Adam.

docs.title: PC Tracking & Discord Setup
docs.text:
To provide the most accurate PC tracking possible, this integration can monitor Steam, Discord, Playnite, and Gaming Status Agent simultaneously and output the result as one "PC" sensor.

Setting up Discord Tracking: Because Home Assistant does not natively track Rich Presence, this integration features a built-in Discord tracker. To use it, you must create a bot in the Developer Portal to read your server's statuses.

  1. Go to the Discord Developer Portal and log in.
  2. Click New Application in the top right corner and give your bot a name (e.g., "Home Assistant Tracker").
  3. On the left menu, click Bot. Scroll down to the Privileged Gateway Intents section.
  4. CRITICAL: You must turn on Presence Intent and Server Members Intent. Without these, the integration cannot see what games you are playing. Save your changes.
  5. Scroll up and click Reset Token. Copy this newly generated Bot Token to a safe place.
  6. On the left menu, click OAuth2, then URL Generator. Under Scopes, check the bot box.
  7. Copy the generated URL at the bottom, paste it into your browser, and authorize the bot to join your personal Discord server.
  8. Open your Discord app, right-click your server icon, and click Copy Server ID (Note: This requires Developer Mode to be enabled in Discord's advanced settings).
  9. Finally, in Home Assistant, add the Gaming Status integration and check Discord in the platforms list — first-time setup then shows a dedicated Discord step for your Bot Token and Server ID. (If already installed, enable Discord under Global Settings and enter them under Advanced.) The integration will automatically fetch a list of your server members so you can easily assign them to your players from a dropdown menu!
  10. Smart Application ID Filtering: Once set up, the integration automatically ignores custom text statuses (like 'Eating dinner' or listening to Spotify). It strictly requires a verified Discord application_id to trigger, guaranteeing only legitimate gaming sessions are captured. Activities relayed by Discord's own Xbox account connection are treated as stale console relays and ignored when the player also has a native Xbox sensor (which is more timely); without one, the relay is still used.
  11. Automation event: Every presence update for a tracked member fires a gaming_status_discord_<member_id> event with {user_id, state, app_id, avatar_url, display_name} (state is the game name, Online, or Offline; display_name is the permanent username).

Setting up Playnite Tracking: Playnite is an incredible open-source library manager that can track games across almost any PC launcher or emulator. To link it to Gaming Status, it utilizes MQTT.

  1. Ensure you have an MQTT Broker (like Mosquitto) installed and configured in Home Assistant.
  2. Open Playnite on your PC, navigate to the Add-ons menu, and install an MQTT broadcasting add-on (e.g., MQTT Client).
  3. Configure the add-on in Playnite with your Home Assistant MQTT broker IP address, username, and password.
  4. In Home Assistant, ensure the MQTT integration detects and creates this binary sensor.
  5. Go to the Gaming Status configuration, select Playnite as an Enabled Platform, and assign that new binary_sensor to your player! By default, it may be named binary_sensor.desktop_playnite_playnite_playing_game.

Setting up Gaming Status Agent Tracking: Gaming Status Agent is a companion Windows tray app that detects what you're playing and which launcher it came from, then publishes it to Home Assistant over MQTT. Home Assistant discovers the sensor automatically, so no YAML is needed. It is the way to track standalone PC games that have no native Home Assistant integration (Epic, GOG, Battle.net, Ubisoft, EA, Amazon Games, and so on). Games it can't detect on its own can be matched by executable or window title under its Custom Games menu; those report their launcher as Custom.

  1. Ensure you have an MQTT Broker (like Mosquitto) installed and the MQTT integration configured in Home Assistant.
  2. Download and run Gaming Status Agent on the PC. Right-click its tray icon, open MQTT Settings, and enter your broker's address and credentials.
  3. Under Platforms, choose which launchers to track. Under Gamertags, optionally enter your account name for each launcher (otherwise your Windows account name is used).
  4. In Home Assistant, confirm the MQTT integration has created sensor.gsa_<profile name> (e.g. sensor.gsa_adam).
  5. Go to the Gaming Status configuration, select Gaming Status Agent as an Enabled Platform, and pick the sensor.gsa_* sensor for your player from the dropdown.

The Agent's sensor reports the following, which Gaming Status reads directly:

Attribute Used for Game Title The current game, or Offline Launcher Launcher Name or None. Shown as the platform (active_platform) on the PC and Master sensors and recorded on each session, so a game played through Epic shows as "Epic" rather than a generic PC entry. Steam and Xbox games are attributed to Steam and Xbox (see below) Profile Name Shown as the player's gamertag for this sensor

Steam and Xbox games from the Agent: the Agent's Steam and Xbox detection is optional and off by default. It's meant for people who want to track those platforms without installing the Steam or Xbox integrations in Home Assistant. Games it reports on those launchers are treated as Steam or Xbox games, not GSA: they show as Steam or Xbox and are recorded on sessions with platform_key steam or xbox. If the native Steam or Xbox sensor is also set up and reports the same game, the Agent steps aside so that sensor's gamertag, achievements, and ratings are used.

The Agent can also report Playnite games, which the priority rules below keep from being counted twice.

Custom sensors: For PCs that can't run Gaming Status Agent (e.g. Linux), enable the Custom platform and select any sensor whose state is the game title, such as a HASS.Agent or template sensor. See Tracking PC Games with a Custom Sensor below. Custom entries that an earlier update moved into the Gaming Status Agent slot are moved back automatically, along with their history.

The PC Sub-Master Priority Logic: If a player launches a game, it is very common for multiple trackers (like Discord, Playnite, and Steam) to detect it simultaneously. To prevent double-counting your playtime hours and sending duplicate push notifications, the sensor.gaming_status_XXXXX_pc sensor uses strict Smart Platform Yielding.

Within the PC sensor, platforms are prioritized in this order: Playnite > Gaming Status Agent > Custom > Steam > Discord. The one exception is a Steam or Xbox game reported by Gaming Status Agent, which always yields to the native Steam or Xbox sensor.

  • Example: If a player launches a Steam game, Discord will likely detect it first and claim the dashboard. Seconds later, when Steam wakes up and detects the same game, Discord will instantly pause its timer and yield control to Steam.
  • Result: You get the lightning-fast notifications of Discord, but the pristine, deduplicated analytics of Steam!

Separately, each platform sensor yields its playtime timer to any higher-priority platform tracking the same game, using the global order Gaming Status Agent > Custom > Steam > Xbox > PlayStation > Playnite > Discord (the same order the Master sensor checks platforms in). The same GSA Steam/Xbox exception applies.

Platform hops: A "finished playing" notification is held for about 45 seconds before sending; if the same game starts on another platform in that window (e.g. one platform's integration briefly drops while another keeps tracking), the end/start notification pair is skipped.

docs.title: Tracking PC Games with a Custom Sensor
docs.text:
If Gaming Status Agent isn't an option (for example on a Linux PC), enable the Custom platform and point the player's Custom slot at any sensor whose state is the game title. A state of on/1/true/playing reports "Unknown Custom Game"; off/0/false/offline/unavailable reports offline. Custom and Gaming Status Agent can be used together; when both report the same game, Gaming Status Agent wins.

A common setup is a HASS.Agent (Windows) or other companion-app "process active" sensor per game, combined into one "PC Funnel" template sensor:

- sensor:
    - name: "Username Active PC Game"
      unique_id: username_active_pc_game
      icon: mdi:desktop-tower
      state: >
        {# Format -> "your_pc_sensor_entity_id": "Clean Dashboard Name" #}
        {% set pc_games = {
          "sensor.pc_name_genshin_impact_status": "Genshin Impact",
          "sensor.pc_name_wonderlands_status": "Tiny Tina's Wonderlands"
        } %}
        {% set active = namespace(game='Offline') %}
        {% for entity_id, game_name in pc_games.items() %}
          {% set state_val = states(entity_id) %}
          {% if state_val in ['on', 'true'] or (state_val | int(default=-1)) > 0 %}
            {% set active.game = game_name %}
          {% endif %}
        {% endfor %}
        {{ active.game }}

Then select sensor.username_active_pc_game as that player's Custom sensor. Custom sensors have no avatar of their own; add custom_username_avatar.png as described in Custom User Avatars.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
docs.text: Below are some of the possible issues you may encounter and their fixes.

docs.title: Checking whether Gaming Status can reach its services
docs.text: Go to Settings → System → Repairs → ⋮ → System information and scroll to Gaming Status. It shows whether Home Assistant can reach the Steam, PlayStation, Xbox and SteamGridDB servers, whether your SteamGridDB API key is working, the result of the last library scans, whether any service has asked Gaming Status to slow down, the number of open repair issues, and (if you use it) whether the Discord bot is connected. These checks only run when you open that page.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: When opening a GitHub issue, please attach the integration's diagnostics: Settings → Devices & services → Gaming Status → ⋮ → Download diagnostics. The file contains your settings, each Gaming Status sensor's current state, library scan results and API rate-limit status. API keys, the NPSSO cookie, the Discord token, account IDs and notification targets are replaced with **REDACTED**, but gamertags and game names are kept. Look it over before posting if you'd rather not share those.

docs.title: Settings → Repairs says my PlayStation NPSSO cookie expired
docs.text: PlayStation Network NPSSO cookies expire after a while, and when that happens PlayStation trophies, ratings and library scans stop updating. Sign in at playstation.com, then open this link in the same browser and copy the npsso value. Paste it into the official PlayStation Network integration (⋮ → Reconfigure), or into PSN NPSSO Override under Gaming Status → Configure → Advanced Settings if you use one. The repair clears itself once PSN accepts the new cookie.

docs.title: My game is being tracked by more than one platform at the same time
docs.text: This generally happens if you're using Discord for tracking along with other services. Sometimes, game titles are reported differently, resulting in a game being tracked by more than one service simultaneously. For example, Xbox may track the title as "DOOM Eternal" while Discord tracks it as "DOOM Eternal (BATTLEMODE)". The solution is to add a game title override under Overrides & Exclusions to normalize the name. This would look like "DOOM Eternal (BATTLEMODE) = DOOM Eternal". Once the names match, the prioritization of trackers will take effect, with Xbox tracking the game and Discord stepping out of the way.

docs.title: My sensor always says "Offline" even when I'm playing!
docs.text: One possibility is the privacy settings of your account. Your online status and game activity must be viewable by the public in order to be properly reported by the Gaming Status integration. Instructions for changing the necessary settings is included below:

docs.title: PlayStation Network (PSN)
docs.text:
Please remember that only the official PlayStation Integration will work properly with Gaming Status; if you have the HACS version installed, uninstall or disable it and install the official integration. If your PSN sensor reports as "Offline" while you are gaming, your PSN privacy settings are likely restricting API access.

On your PS5 Console:

  • Go to Settings > Users and Accounts > Privacy.
  • Select View and Customize Your Privacy Settings.
  • Scroll down to your activity and locate the option for "Who can see your online status and what you're currently playing".
  • Change this setting to Anyone.

Note on Hidden Games: In the same Privacy menu, check the "Hide your games from other players" setting. Any game toggled to be hidden in this list will refuse to broadcast its title to Home Assistant.

docs.title: Steam
docs.text:
Steam separates your overall profile visibility from your gaming activity. If "Game details" are restricted, Home Assistant will see you as online but will not know what game you are playing and report you as "Offline".

Global Privacy Settings:

  • Go to your Steam Profile in the desktop client or web browser.
  • Click Edit Profile, then navigate to the Privacy Settings tab.
  • Ensure My profile is set to Public.
  • Ensure Game details is set to Public. This specific setting controls whether you are seen as "in-game" and broadcasts the title of the software you are running.

Per-Game Privacy: Steam allows you to mark individual games as private. If a specific game is not showing up, right-click the game in your Steam Library, click the gear icon on the game details page, and go to Privacy to ensure it is not marked as a private game.

docs.title: Xbox / Microsoft
docs.text:
Xbox possesses highly granular privacy controls that explicitly separate your online status from your game history. Both must be publicly visible for the integration to function properly.

Via Web Browser (Recommended):

  • Sign in to Xbox.com and click your gamerpic in the top-right corner of the page.
  • Click "..." (More options) > Xbox settings > Privacy & online safety > Privacy.
  • Under the "Others can" section, find "Others can see if you're online" and set it to Everyone.
  • Find "Others can see your game and app history" and set it to Everyone.
  • Scroll to the bottom and click Submit to save your changes.

Via Xbox Console:

  • Press the Xbox button to open the guide, then go to Profile & system > Settings.
  • Navigate to Account > Privacy & online safety > Xbox privacy > View details & customize.
  • Select Online status & history.
  • Ensure both "Others can see if you're online" and "Others can see your game and app history" are set to allow visibility.

For PC Gamers:

  • If you are playing non-Xbox games on a Windows PC, open the Game Bar by pressing the Windows key + G.
  • Go to the Xbox Social widget, click Xbox Social Options in the title bar, then select Account.
  • Under "Others can see your PC game activity", ensure this is set to Allow so that Microsoft can collect your PC game activity and determine what you are playing.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text:
Discord requires specific settings to be enabled on both your local client and the specific server where your Home Assistant bot resides. If your status is not updating, Discord is likely refusing to broadcast your Rich Presence data.

Client Activity Privacy:

  • Open Discord and click the gear icon (User Settings) in the bottom left.
  • Navigate to Activity Privacy under the Activity Settings section.
  • Ensure Display current activity as a status message is toggled ON. This is the master switch that allows Discord to broadcast what game you are playing.

Server-Specific Privacy: Even if your global activity is enabled, Discord allows you to hide your status from specific servers. If your bot is on a server where your activity is hidden, it will not be able to track your games.

  • Open the Discord server where your Home Assistant bot is located.
  • Click the Server Name at the top left of the screen to open the dropdown menu.
  • Select Privacy Settings.
  • Ensure Activity Status is toggled ON to allow your gaming activity to be visible within that specific server.

Note on Custom Games: If you manually added a non-supported game to Discord via the "Registered Games" menu, ensure the eye icon next to the game is not crossed out. If it is crossed out, Discord will hide that specific game from your status.

docs.title: The game cover art is missing or incorrect.
docs.text:
The integration searches SteamGridDB for high-quality cover art based on the name of the game. If a publisher names a game weirdly on Xbox (like "Call of Duty®: HQ - Cross-Gen Bundle"), the search will fail.

  • The Fix: Use the Game Title Overrides in the Advanced Settings section to map that messy title to a clean one (e.g., Call of Duty®: HQ - Cross-Gen Bundle = Call of Duty). The integration will instantly find the right art!

docs.title: My gamerpic / avatar is blank or broken.
docs.text:
Sometimes, official APIs (especially PlayStation) fail to pass the avatar image URL to Home Assistant.

  • The Fix (Local Override): You can force your own profile picture! Create a folder inside your Home Assistant www directory called gaming_status. Drop a .png or .jpg image in there using the format: [platform]_[profile_name]_avatar.jpg.
  • Example: If your profile name is "Player One" and you want an Xbox avatar, name the file xbox_player_one_avatar.jpg and the integration will automatically use it!

docs.title: My Epic / GOG / other PC game isn't triggering.
docs.text:
PC games outside Steam and Xbox are tracked by Gaming Status Agent.

  • Check the Agent first: Right-click its tray icon and choose Run Diagnostics. It shows what it currently detects and why, and which launchers are switched on under Platforms.
  • Check the sensor: In Home Assistant, sensor.gsa_<profile name> should show the game title and a Launcher attribute. If it doesn't exist, check the Agent's MQTT settings and that the MQTT integration is set up.
  • Check the player: Make sure Gaming Status Agent is an enabled platform and that the player's Gaming Status Agent slot points at that sensor.gsa_* sensor.

docs.title: I changed a game's title, but the old name is still showing.
docs.text: The Master Sensor caches history and states to prevent drop-outs. If things look stuck, simply restart Home Assistant to flush the cache and force it to rebuild from the current live data.
